newsitem.title: UK: Rachmaninov love letters expected to fetch $29,000.
newsitem.headline: Rachmaninov love letters expected to fetch $29,000.

text.p: Intimate love letters from Russian composer Sergei Rachmaninov to a young woman journalist are expected to sell for more than 17,000 pounds ($29,000) when they are put up for auction, London firm Sotheby's said on Monday.

The letters to Marietta Shaginyan, a journalist who later published a poetry anthology, date from 1912 to 1917. They reveal a tender side to Rachmaninov, composer of supremely romantic music but personally an aloof figure.
"Rachmaninov wrote very few letters -- they are very rare," said Simon Maguire, an expert on musical manuscripts at auctioneers Sotherby's.
"The letters are remarkable because they tell you a great deal about his lack of self-confidence," he said by telephone.
Rachmaninov (1873-1943) was one of the most most popular composers of the 20th century but little is known about his personality.
"Besides my children, music and flowers, I love you...," he wrote to Shaginyan in Russian. "It is true that I do not believe in myself."
The composer, who was married to his cousin, left Russia during the revolution and never returned. The correspondence with Shaginyan ended with his departure.
Maguire said he was not discouraged after love letters written by Boris Pasternak, whose "Doctor Zhivago" is a classic of Russian literature, failed to reach their reserve price at auction last week.
He did not expect the earlier auction to influence the Rachmaninov sale on Friday. "It's a completely different market," Maguire said.
